label: first occurrence of b/e/0/w/g/m late in the original phase, after several 1/x/f/r/n/z/s/v/j-type tokens
explanation: Fires only in the original (input) phase, from step 3 on (none at t<=1; it peaks at t=5-7, and the per-step rate rises with L). It never fires on the delimiter or during copy. It is input-token selective: b (26% of mass), e (19%), 0 (16%), w (14%), g, m, and a little on z and o; it is nearly silent on a, u, k and most other tokens. It mostly fires on the first occurrence of that token (91% of mass). Whether it fires on a given b/e/0/w step depends on the earlier prefix: prefixes heavy in 1, x, f, r, n, z, s, v, j (first token x or 1 gives a 2-3.5x lift) make it more likely, which suggests it reads a distributed hidden-state context that is not cleanly captured. The token-identity-plus-position rule alone covers about 80% of mass but with precision near 0.2; adding the prefix-count condition raises precision to about 0.33 at about 74% mass recall. The magnitude claims are taken only from the profile tables: b carries the largest share, and the top activations (max 0.15) are b/e/0 steps after prefixes containing 1/x/f.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: b, e, 0, w, g, m; least: s, h, r, d) and the first original token (most: x, 1, r, s, v, n; least: g, w, e, b); timing cues that raise it most: t=5, t=6, t=4.
